newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Euros yield, Bradys yawn.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Euros yield, Bradys yawn.

text.p: Brazil debt watchers said they see some value in high-yielding Eurobonds this week, but expect little interest in the nation's Brady bonds, which continue to underperform neighboring Mexico and Argentina.

IN SECONDARY TRADE, Brazilian Eurobonds tightened five basis points on average last week. Traders said new money flowed into high-risk bonds, which helped Tevecap's 12.625 percent due 2004 ZRIT tighten 10 basis points to 520 bp over Treasuries.
Telecom's 10.75 percent due 2004 ZUWD also did well, narrowing 11 bp to 315 over. The bond has been as tight as 290 bp over Treasuries and is guaranteed by federally owned telephone
Traders saw room for tightening in both issues.

Netsat's 12.75 percent due 2001, however, held at about 530 bp over, on poor earnings and sales growth. Although the issue has traded as tight as 330 bp over, market players said they would avoid it until the company showed steadier signs of improvement.

ON THE SOVEREIGN SIDE, Brazil's 8.875 percent due 2001 ZQ4P, its five-year global, tightened 10 basis points to 171 bp over Treasuries. Despite the gain, the bond still looked attractive against Argentina's five-year global, the 9.25 percent due 2001 NZ4D, which also narrowed by 10 bp to 150 over.

Emerging market debt watchers, for the second week in a row, recommended getting out of Argentina 2001 this week and into either Brazil 2001 or Mexico's 9.75 percent due 2001 ZM5W, which widened five bp to 160 bp over the five year U.S. Treasury bill.

IN THE PRIMARY MARKET, Banco BMC on Monday set its $50 million eight-year step-up Eurobond, with both puts and calls after three and five years, via lead manager West Merchant Bank. The bond has a 10.25 percent coupon to the first put, then steps up to 10.50 percent between the third and fifth year and up to 10.75 percent to maturity.
When priced to the three-year put, the bond gives a spread of 395 bp over Treasuries. Price talk had been between 380 bp to 410 bp over.

Furnas priced a $90 million eight-year bond ZXLW last week. The issue has a 9.0 percent coupon and was launced at 243 bp over Treasuries when priced to the five-year put. It tightened to 239 bp over by Friday's close, traders said.

BRADY BOND TRADING was expected to be pinched this week by the yen's recent gains against the dollar. Some Treasury watchers fear a narrowing of the spread between U.S. and Japanese interest rates will draw Japanese investors out of the U.S. Treasury market.

"There are no (Brady) trades that jump to mind now," said Tina Vandersteel, a fixed-income analyst for JP Morgan in Brazil. She said the market would be docile at least through mid-week, when the U.S. government is expected to release consumer and producer price figures.

ON THE LOCAL FRONT, the market sees little reason for enthusiasm following the May 6 auction of a controlling share of state mining giant CVRD. Now Brazil watchers will focus on civil service reforms, but players are not excited about the short-term prospects.

"We have heard so much for so long about the reforms with no real progress. The feeling is that they are pretty bogged down with reforms and it will be a while before anybody is going to buy on this basis," said a Brady bond trader in New York.
